newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Illiquid Czech Zivno stock a hold-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Illiquid Czech Zivno stock a hold-analysts.

text.p: Czech analysts say low liquidity in Zivnostenska Banka a.s. shares on the Prague Stock Exchange limits their recommendation for the stock to a "hold" despite signs the issue is fundamentally undervalued.

"Liquidity of shares is, after all, very much lower than other banking issues," said Josef Kovalovsky, analyst at Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka. "In view of the low liquidity... we are recommending to hold (Zivno shares)."
Zivno is the Czech Republic's sixth largest bank, and it is the first in terms of dividend yield per share price, which was 5.6 percent at Tuesday's price of 2,680 crowns, down 10 crowns from Friday.
The bank paid a 160 crown gross dividend on 1995 profits, and analysts expect it to rise to about 170 crowns this year on net profit rising to between 435 and 440 million crowns.
"I expect net profit of 435 to 440 millions in 1996," said Josef Kovalovsky, an analyst with Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s.(CSOB).
The bank itself has said its net earnings would rise around six percent to 430 million crowns. In the first half of 1996, its net grew to 268 million crowns from 207 over the same period of 1995.
The bank is known for its conservative lending policy which has led to an extremely low percentage of risky credits which now comprise only about one percent of Zivno's total loan portfolio.
Zivno also specialises in financing of foreign trade and in foreign exchange operations.

The bank is majority owned by strategic investors, leaving little of its equity on the market. The largest shareholders are BHF Bank AG with 47 percent and the International Finance Corporation (IFC) with 10 porcent.

Insurer Ceska Pojistovna a.s. and its investment arm Kapitalova Investicni Spolecnost a.s. hold 6.5 percent, the privatisation agency National Property Fund and Credit Commercial de France (CCF) have five percent each.

This structure leaves only some 350,000 1,000-crowns denominated shares on the market, restricting liquidity in the issue to level below that of other banks and keeping Zivno price, along with bank IPB a.s., one of the most stable issues on the stock market.
Milan Kucera of Akro Capital said that "the expected privatisation of our largest banks will probably not influence the price" as the bank was virtually fully private.
"Significant price fluctuations could be expected if IFC or NPF sell out," added Leos Jirman of BH Securities.
Most analysts added that Zivno would be "hold" at 2,700, or a long-term buy, especially if the stock falls under 2,650 crowns.
